title: [ownership][diagnostics] no §28.2 use-after-dispose warning at a FIELD STORE through an explicitly-disposed binding (`a.Dispose(); a.f := new Q();`)
body:
**Shape.** A slot store through a binding killed by a dominating `Dispose()`.

```bezel
var a := new R(new Q());
a.Dispose();
a.f := new Q();      // a read of `a` (K1.5: the holder) after a dominating kill — §28.2's mandatory warning is missing
```

**Measured on r35.** Both modes compile with **no diagnostic**; `--checked-disposal` raises `DisposedAccessException` at the store (exit 70), so the runtime backstop is in place and only the compile-time warning is missing. The same program with `a.Use();` or `var b := a.f;` in place of the store draws `use of \`a\` after a dominating explicit Dispose() call … (§28.2)`.

**Spec (v0.345).** K1 (§28.3.1), *explicitly-disposed*: *"a straight-line read falls under §28.2's use-after-dispose warning regime"*; §28.2: *"Under a dominating kill every use in the list above draws this warning"* — a field store evaluates the holder (K9.5: receiver first) and is a use of it. Expected: the warning at `a.f := …`.

**Differential numbers.** 15 of 6,000 sampled programs (fields fragment and all-features sample, vars 3 / len 4): every model-warned `fst` through a dominated-disposed holder compiles silently on r35.

**Measured on r35** (`bezelc 0.0.0-f6863e62`, the 2026-10-27 release build; main may have moved since). Found by the model-vs-compiler differential (`scratch/bzdiff`, proposal 0047 §5.3 / soundness README §3.2).
